title: Derived-to-ordinary reduction comparison for finite scalar local models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_F$ with its $\ell$-adic topology, and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V$ be any scheme on its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Put $B_V=p_V^*\underline A$, where the coefficient ring on the point is the condensed ring of continuous $A$-valued functions [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Work with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $M$ be a $B_V$-module with a finite constant scalar local model: on a pro-étale cover $\{U_i\to V\}$ it is $B_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{P_i}$ for finitely presented scalar $A$-modules $P_i$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible].
For $n\ge1$ form the strict tower complexes
$$D_n=[M\xrightarrow{\pi^n}M]\quad\text{in degrees }-1,0,\qquad Q_n=(M/\pi^nM)[0].$$
The transition $D_{n+1}\to D_n$ is $(\pi,1)$, and that of $Q$ is the actual quotient map [def-weil-inverse-system]. There is a strict map $e:D_\bullet\to Q_\bullet$, zero in degree $-1$ and the quotient in degree $0$. With total right derived inverse limit on strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], the canonical map
$$R\varprojlim e:R\varprojlim_n D_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n Q_n$$
is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category. It is natural for every actual $B_V$-module map between such models. The augmentation $M[0]\to D_n$ is the identity in degree $0$; under this isomorphism its derived-limit map is the one induced by the actual quotient augmentation $M[0]\to Q_n$. Scalar torsion is allowed, with no global bound on the torsion exponents of the local models, and no quasi-compactness, Noetherianity or invertibility of $\ell$ is assumed. The assertion is a comparison of two limits, not a levelwise identification of derived and ordinary reductions, and does not itself assert completeness of $M$.

proof.text: Work on one member $U_i$ of the model cover, and write $P=P_i$. Finite presentation gives a surjection $v:A^r\to P$ with $r$ finite. The valuation-ring theorem makes $A$ a DVR. Apply Smith normal form to $N=\ker v\subset A^r$: there are bases $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $A^r$ and $w_1,\ldots,w_s$ of $N$, $s\le r$, with $w_j=a_je_j$. Each $a_j$ is nonzero because $w_j$ is a basis vector of the submodule. Write $a_j=u_j\pi^{b_j}$ with $u_j$ a unit and $b_j\ge0$ by the DVR factorization theorem; rescaling the corresponding basis vector absorbs $u_j$. Thus the specified surjection fits into $0\to A^s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{diag}(\pi^{b_j})}A^r\xrightarrow{v}P\to0$. Taking the cokernel coordinate by coordinate gives $P\cong A^{r-s}\oplus\bigoplus_{j=1}^s A/(\pi^{b_j})$. A summand with $b_j=0$ is zero; $s=0$ and $r=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final assertion; the existing Smith-normal-form leaf supplies the diagonal bases.

proof.text: Put $B=B_{U_i}$. The integral quotient normalization states that $B$ is flat over the discrete constant scalar ring sheaf and that multiplication by every positive power of $\pi$ on $B$ is injective. Use the finite-constant-model meaning of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: its scalar $A$ and $P$ are constant sheaves acting through the scalar map into $B$. The exact constant finite-free presentation theorem applied to the short exact sequence in step 1 identifies $M|_{U_i}$ with the cokernel of the same diagonal matrix over $B$. Consequently $M|_{U_i}\cong B^{r-s}\oplus\bigoplus_j B/\pi^{b_j}B$. Let $c_i=\max(\{1\}\cup\{b_j\})$. Every kernel $K_n|_{U_i}=\ker(\pi^n:M|_{U_i}\to M|_{U_i})$ lies in the displayed quotient summands, since the free summand has zero kernel. Those summands are all killed by $\pi^{c_i}$. Hence $\pi^{c_i}K_n|_{U_i}=0$ for every $n\ge1$. The decomposition is used only to establish this bound, not to define any comparison morphism.

source.place: Tags 093J (lemma-constant-exact) and 093M (lemma-completion-flat); apply the cited normalized coefficient and finite-presentation statements.

proof.text: Globally define $K_n=\ker(\pi^n:M\to M)$, with transition multiplication by $\pi$. This is well defined since $\pi^n(\pi x)=\pi^{n+1}x$. For the strict map $e_n:D_n\to Q_n$, the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $C_n=\operatorname{Cone}(e_n)$ as $[M\xrightarrow{-\pi^n}M\xrightarrow{q_n}M/\pi^nM]$ in degrees $-2,-1,0$. The inclusion $K_n[2]\to C_n$ into degree $-2$ is a quasi-isomorphism: its cohomology in degree $-2$ is $K_n$, in degree $-1$ is $\ker(q_n)/\pi^nM=0$, and in degree $0$ is $\operatorname{coker}(q_n)=0$. The cone transition is $(\pi,1,\bar q_n)$ in these three degrees. Therefore these inclusions commute strictly with the kernel-tower transitions. In particular a zero transition of the kernel tower gives a zero transition of the cone tower in the derived category. All assertions remain true after exact slice restriction.

source.place: Tag 05RU (definition-derived-category); direct calculation with the cone convention and exact restriction of the cited slice theorem.

proof.text: On the slice at $U_i$, the transition $K_{n+c_i}|_{U_i}\to K_n|_{U_i}$ is exactly multiplication by $\pi^{c_i}$, and is zero by step 2. The compatible quasi-isomorphisms in step 3 thus show that $C_{n+c_i}|_{U_i}\to C_n|_{U_i}$ is zero in the ordinary derived category. Apply the strict-tower homotopy-limit theorem on this small ringed slice site to $e|_{U_i}$. Its cone-tower criterion gives that the actual morphism $R\varprojlim(e|_{U_i})$ is an isomorphism. This uses derived products as in that theorem, without asserting exactness of ordinary countable products or replacing the derived limit by a termwise limit.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), combined with the pro-zero cone criterion of the cited strict-tower theorem.

proof.text: The natural slice/strict-derived-limit isomorphism of [lem-sp-slice-restriction-strict-derived-limit], applied to the strict morphism $e$, identifies the restriction of $R\varprojlim e$ with $R\varprojlim(e|_{U_i})$. Both its source and target are the ordinary uncompleted derived objects used throughout. The latter map is invertible for every $i$ by step 4. Joint conservativity of pro-étale cover restriction for condensed module complexes therefore makes $R\varprojlim e$ invertible on $V$. There is no maximum of the $c_i$ in this argument: each is used solely on its own slice. The empty scheme case is covered as well, since cover restriction is jointly conservative there and the module category is zero.

source.place: Lemma 4.5, proof, conservativity of cover restriction; the cited slice theorem supplies compatibility with strict derived inverse limit.

proof.text: For an actual $B_V$-linear map $f:M\to M'$, use $(f,f)$ on $D_n$ and the induced quotient map $\bar f_n$ on $Q_n$. The identities $f\pi^n=\pi^nf$, $q'_nf=\bar f_nq_n$ show that these are chain maps, commute with $(\pi,1)$ and the quotient transitions, and satisfy $e'_nD_n(f)=Q_n(f)e_n$. Thus they form a commutative square of strict towers. Applying the functor $R\varprojlim$ gives the asserted naturality of its isomorphism. The chain augmentation $a_n:M[0]\to D_n$ is the identity in degree $0$ and satisfies $e_na_n=q_n$ exactly. This equality is compatible with transitions, so the same derived functor sends it to the equality of maps from the derived limit of the constant $M[0]$ tower. Precompose with the canonical $M[0]\to R\varprojlim\operatorname{const}(M[0])$, induced by the diagonal/limit adjunction and the right-derived unit. It gives $(R\varprojlim e)\,a_D=a_Q$. Thus the compared augmentations are the ones from the actual quotient maps; the proof does not need to identify the derived limit of the constant tower with $M[0]$.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), functorial strict-tower model; explicit chain-map and coaugmentation equalities.

split_report.summary: Six steps: diagonal scalar presentation over the DVR, local uniform torsion-kernel bound, strict cone/kernel quasi-isomorphism, pro-zero slice comparison, cover-local gluing, and explicit map/augmentation naturality. Reuses existing nodes only. Statement retained; no completeness, quasi-compactness or global torsion bound is introduced.
split_report.blueprint: Makes precise the integral finite-model comparison used underneath det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle, Refinement isomorphisms, through det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement (2); the current blueprint contains no explicit proof of this reduction-comparison input.

tool_uses.why: Generic coefficient-ring theorem used only to establish the DVR hypothesis for scalar Smith normal form; no compactification argument is replaced.
Generic normalized integral coefficient theorem provides flatness over constant scalars and injectivity of powers of the uniformizer on any scheme; no unit statement otherwise provides those facts.
Generic exact constant presentation theorem identifies the local scalar presentation with the same matrix over the coefficient sheaf; it does not replace a compactification step.
Generic strict derived-limit functor and pro-zero cone criterion, already needed in the item statement; used without proper-base-change hypotheses.
Generic ringed-slice theorem permits the comparison to be checked separately on each model slice without a global torsion bound.
Generic cover-local detection theorem for ordinary condensed module derived categories glues the slice comparisons; no compactification route is replaced.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q16-af8ff321a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item's statement and all six steps, plus the statement of every cited node. There are no new nodes. The item is still unsplit on live and on side-live, and its statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to live. There is no repair note, so this is not a re-split. The statement is true and not weakened. I tested P=0, P=A^r, P=A/π^b (where the levelwise comparison fails but the limits agree) and an infinite union with no common exponent. The parent (step 4 of lem-sfb-supported-integral-model-restriction-tower) uses exactly the isomorphism, its compatibility with the augmentations, and naturality. Step 1: finite presentation, the DVR theorem (clauses 2 and 4), the Smith normal form leaf and the unit-times-uniformizer-power leaf (Noetherian local domain with m=πB) give 0→A^s→A^r→P→0 with the diagonal matrix diag(π^{b_j}); a_j≠0 because it multiplies a basis vector. Step 2: the normalization node applied to U_i (B flat over the constant sheaf A, π^j injective) and the constant presentation node on (U_i)_proet give M|U_i ≅ B^{r-s}⊕⊕B/π^{b_j}, which matches the meaning in sk-def-sfb-constructible(1). So π^{c_i} kills K_n|U_i for every n. Step 3: I recomputed the cone with C(f)^r=L^r⊕K^{r+1}, d=[[d_L,f],[0,-d_K]]. It is [M -π^n→ M -q_n→ M/π^n], K_n[2]→C_n is a quasi-isomorphism, and the transitions (π,1,q̄) commute with the kernel transitions. Step 4: on the small slice site, the strict-tower node's cone criterion applies with the transition from n+c_i to n. Step 5: the natural slice/R lim isomorphism, applied to the morphism e, plus cover conservativity for any condensed ring, scheme and pro-étale family; no global torsion bound is used. Step 6: an elementary equality of strict maps gives naturality and (R lim e)a_D=a_Q. Sources checked: Stacks 00PD, 093J, 093M, 0941 and 05RU (tags present, 093J and 0941 text read); HRS Lemma 4.5 (proof, conservativity); the latest blueprint's det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement (2) and the cocycle proof's Refinement isomorphisms paragraph. The blueprint gives no explicit argument, so proof_origin=agent is correct. lean.statement: theorem finiteScalarOrdinaryQuotientComparison (L : DerivedCategory.{w} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Modules l E V) ⥤ DerivedCategory.{w} (Modules l E V)) (η : limitComplex (A := Modules l E V) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ L) [L.IsRightDerivedFunctor η (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Modules l E V) (.up ℤ))] : (∀ (M : Modules l E V), HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (IntegralQuotient.integral l E) V M → IsIso (L.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map (comparison (scalar l E V) M)))) ∧ (∀ (M N : Modules l E V), HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (IntegralQuotient.integral l E) V M → HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (IntegralQuotient.integral l E) V N → ∀ f : M ⟶ N, L.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map (derivedMap (scalar l E V) f)) ≫ L.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map (comparison (scalar l E V) N)) = L.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map (comparison (scalar l E V) M)) ≫ L.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map (quotientMap (scalar l E V) f))) ∧ (∀ (M : Modules l E V), HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (IntegralQuotient.integral l E) V M → limitUnit L η M (derivedUnit (scalar l E V) M) ≫ L.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map (comparison (scalar l E V) M)) = limitUnit L η M (quotientUnit (scalar l E V) M))
lean.note: The strict source and constant target towers carry one natural scalar-power morphism. Its cone and its categorical cokernel in the abelian tower category give the specified D and Q, including actual quotient transitions. The right-derived functor is quantified with its canonical universal-property unit; no arbitrary comparison map or completeness assumption is used. Generic abelian-category helpers are specialized to the published integral module-object category, retaining the small site universes.
